show: Bigfoot and Beyond with Cliff and Bobo

einzeiler: A deep dive into the unsung heroes, pioneers, and foundational researchers of Bigfoot…
kurzfassung: The hosts examine the foundational figures of Bigfoot research, often referred to as the four horsemen, and debate who else deserves recognition across different eras. They highlight lesser-known investigators, field researchers, and archivists whose past work built the bedrock of modern cryptozoology. Throughout the discussion, they emphasize the importance of acknowledging these historical contributors before their stories are forgotten.
stichpunkte: Assigning the original four horsemen roles based on the personalities of John Green, Grover Krantz, Rene de Hinden, and Peter Byrne
Recognizing Roger Patterson's extensive field contributions and his role as a pioneer of call blasting beyond just the famous film
Debating the impact of Bob Gimlin's personal integrity versus the physical evidence associated with the Patterson-Gimlin film
Honoring the San Francisco Bay Area Bigfoot Research Group for producing enduring data and early newsletters
Highlighting regional researchers like Jim Heuchan and Don Keating who advanced investigations outside the Pacific Northwest
Examining the influence of modern researchers, field study leaders like Daryl Collier, and the cultural shift caused by Finding Bigfoot

clips.hook: Why Grover Krantz is the obvious choice for the horseman of death
clips.text: One of the original figures is assigned a grim title because he arranged for his remains to be studied in decomposition facilities and his skeleton donated to a museum alongside his dog.

clips.hook: A statistical bias that might explain why an early researcher was wrong
clips.text: A psychological tendency causes people to gravitate toward choices that resemble their own names, which could jokingly account for why an investigator incorrectly believed certain creatures possessed foot arches.

clips.hook: Holding the first conferences outside the Pacific Northwest
clips.text: An investigator achieved lasting significance by sustaining regional inquiries, investigating numerous reports, and organizing early gatherings far from the traditional West Coast hotspots.

clips.hook: How a popular television series shifted the cultural landscape
clips.text: A mainstream television program transformed public awareness and social consciousness around the topic far beyond what niche documentaries or regional media had previously achieved.

clips.hook: The surprising everyday invention created by a famous footprint caster
clips.text: The individual famous for securing the initial footprint casts also designed a specialized mechanical device utilized in harvesting Christmas trees.

beschreibung:
Originally recorded and released as an exclusive members-only episode back in April of 2024, this discussion between Cliff Barackman, James "Bobo" Fay, and Matt Pruitt focuses on a few of the researchers whom they consider to be unsung heroes or additions to the "Horsemen of Sasquatchery!"

See Cliff and Pruitt at Cryptid Con in Florence, IN, November 21-22!

Sign up for our weekly bonus podcast "Beyond Bigfoot & Beyond" and ad-free episodes!

Here's the list of people mentioned in the episode:

1.0 (1950s-1960s): Roger Patterson, Bob Titmus

2.0 (1970s-1980s): The Bay Area Group, Jim Hewkin, Don Keating, Ron Morehead, Richard Greenwell, Loren Coleman

3.0 (1990s-2000s): Matt Moneymaker, Doug Hajicek, Jeff Meldrum, John Bindernagel, Henner Fahrenbach, Derek Randles

4.0 (2010s-2020s): Clobo, Daryl Colyer, The Olympic Project, Small Town Monsters

Unsung Heroes: Dennis Jensen, Dennis Pfohl, Wally Hersom, Thom Shay, Wes Summerlin, Vance Orchard, Will Duncan, JDL, Tal H. Branco, Erwin Supple, Jim McClarin

International Horsefolk: Dimitri Bayanov, Marie-Jeanne Koffmann, Jordi Magraner, Dean Harrison

Honorable Mentions: Tom Yamarone, Betty Allen, Jerry Crew, Daniel Perez, Todd Prescott, Tom Steenburg
